title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion: Cocatalyst Design Principles and Mechanistic Insights from Electrocatalysis
content:
Photoelectrochemical nitrate‐to‐ammonia conversion offers a sustainable route for ammonia production by utilizing solar energy. This Review highlights how mechanistic insights and catalyst design principles established in electrocatalytic nitrate reduction can guide cocatalyst engineering for PEC systems, providing perspectives for developing efficient, selective, and durable photoelectrodes for solar‐driven ammonia synthesis.








ABSTRACT
Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO3RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO3RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO3RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO3RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO3RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH3 synthesis.

title: Gravity‐Differential Modulated Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Continuous and Stable Energy Harvesting From Disordered Vibrations
content:
A gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced triboelectric energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG harvests forms a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time.








ABSTRACT
Low‐frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self‐powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double‐sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM‐TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long‐term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM‐TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self‐powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.

title: Molecular Architecture of Non‑Fullerene Acceptors Balances Homo‐ and Hetero‐Intermolecular Interactions to Enhance Thermal Stability of Organic Photovoltaics
content:
Experimental and theoretical studies of 28 non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) reveal how molecular structures of NFAs govern intermolecular interactions and thermal stability of bulk‐heterojunction blends, providing guidance for the development of thermally resilient organic photovoltaics.








ABSTRACT
High‐efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor‐acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk‐heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo‐ and hetero‐intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well‐known indacenodithieno[3,2‐b]thiophene‐based (ITIC‐series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene‐based (IEICO‐series) acceptors, and state‐of‐the‐art Y‐series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo‐interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine‐tune their hetero‐interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo‐interactions while minimizing hetero‐interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature‐reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo‐ and hetero‐interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.

title:
Light Ignites Lattice
Oxygen in an Asymmetric Motif
content:
Abstract
Lattice-oxygen-mediated pathways bypass the energy-intensive steps that constrain adsorbate-mediated catalysis. Activating these pathways under mild conditions, however, means breaking metal–oxygen bonds that are, by design, strong. Asymmetric M1-O-M2 motifs, in which a bridging oxygen sits between two cations of different electronic character, decouple oxygen activation from oxygen release by distributing these functions across chemically distinct sites. Here, we show that a Cu-doped In2O3 system with a well-defined asymmetric Cu–O–In unit exhibits enhanced photoinduced lattice oxygen activity. Series (quasi) in situ spectroscopy captures the activation, consumption, and replenishment of lattice oxygen under illumination in real time. Photogenerated carriers populate around the Cu–O site preferentially, weakening the Cu–O bond enough to extract lattice oxygen at room temperature. The optimized material, Cui-In2O3, gives a response of 32.4 toward 5 ppm of H2S under visible light. The results connect local coordination asymmetry directly to photoinduced oxygen functionality and suggest a route toward photodriven catalysts built around asymmetric oxygen sites.

title:
Simulating
Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based
Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
content:
Abstract
Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton-exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl– + CH3Cl), and proton-transfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O···H+···OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware/noise-models show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware. These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.

title:
Leveraging Cubenes
to Access Highly Functionalized
Fused Cubes
content:
Abstract
Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.

title:
Structural Rigidity
Enables Amplified Spontaneous
Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
content:
Abstract
Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

title:
An “Unachievable”
Molecular Sieve with
Sole Six-Membered Rings
content:
Abstract
The frameworks of zeolite molecular sieves constructed from a sole type of ring, such as 6-membered rings (6MRs), are regarded as unachievable structures that would not even be found in hypothetical zeolite databases containing tens of millions of structures. Herein, we for the first time report a novel aluminophosphate ZJM-11 molecular sieve, with a fully 6-membered ring (6MR) framework, which was successfully obtained from topotactic transformation. The obtained structure, which possesses fully opened micropores, represents a rare case of a single-ring zeolite topology with an ultrahigh framework density, viewed from the perspective of conventional wisdom as an “unachievable” molecular sieve. Advanced characterizations unveil the dynamic framework reconstruction mediated by ZJM-9 and/or ZJM-10 intermediates, pinpointing this structural evolution as the essential step toward ZJM-11 formation. This work therefore delivers critical knowledge for the rational design of unconventional zeolite molecular sieves.

title:
A Multiscale Theoretical
Framework of Piezocatalysis
content:
Abstract
Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical stimuli into chemical energy, holds significant promise for noninvasive medical therapies. In this process, ultrasonic frequency plays a dual role: it governs both the reaction rate and the electromechanical coupling efficiency, thereby serving as a critical bridge between microscopic and macroscopic physical processes. However, conventional theoretical models lack a multiscale description of coupled physical processes and thus fail to reveal how frequency dictates catalytic activity. Here, we develop an integrated multiscale framework that links, for the first time, macroscopic bubble cavitation dynamics, mesoscopic piezoelectric constitutive relations, and microscopic chemical reaction rate─with ultrasonic frequency as the unifying thread. Our model uncovers the complete frequency-dependent activity profile and elucidates the physical origin of an optimal frequency, predicting a volcano-shaped activity-frequency relationship that agrees well with a range of experimental reports. By reinterpreting piezocatalysis from a multiscale physical field perspective, this work establishes a new theoretical paradigm for the rational design of piezocatalysts.

title:
Benzaldehyde
Is the Redox Mediator for Aerobic C–N
Cleavage in Epoxy Composite Recycling
content:
Abstract
Chemical methods are promising avenues to recycle fiber-reinforced polymer waste. Here, we reintroduce tripotassium phosphate-mediated benzyl alcohol conditions for epoxy cleavage. While these conditions were developed in 2008 for anhydride-cured epoxy cleavage and have been applied to amine-linked epoxy cleavage, no account has been made of why these conditions should work with the latter, or why air exposure appears critical for their success. We now show how benzaldehyde, formed in situ from benzyl alcohol, plays the crucial redox role that enables selective C–N bond cleavage: tertiary amines are cleaved by a previously uncharacterized mechanism in which benzaldehyde facilitates iminium formation from the polymer’s C–N linkage. Subsequent hydrolysis and base-promoted elimination cleave the C═N and C–O bonds, respectively, enabling the recovery of bisphenol A and release of the linking diamines. Carbon fiber (CF) and even glass fiber (GF) fabrics are preserved, and recovered CF fabrics are remanufactured into second-generation composites with near-virgin quality and mechanical performance. These mechanistic insights may inform the future development of selective diamine recovery strategies from thermosets, which is a challenge when valorizing composites. Collectively, these results present promising recycling conditions with the potential to valorize matrices and fibers from a wide range of composites, spanning high-performance carbon fiber to widely used fiberglass.

title:
Solvent-Dipole
Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis
Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from
Biomass
content:
Abstract
5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.

title:
Single-Water Microsolvation
Promotes Proton Sharing
in a Neutral Formic Acid–Ammonia Complex
content:
Abstract
Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.

title:
A Tumor-Activatable
DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates
NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor
Cytotoxicity
content:
Abstract
Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.

title:
Stabilization and Transformation
of MXenes into Flexible
and Thermal Oxidation-Resistant Non-van der Waals solids via Vapor-Phase
Chemical Intercalation
content:
Abstract
Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) solids derived from MXenes exhibit attractive physical and chemical properties but are usually limited by the irreversible phase transformation of MXenes into rocksalt structures at high temperatures. Herein, we develop a vapor-phase chemical intercalation strategy mediated by high-vapor-pressure zinc (Zn) to efficiently stabilize the transition metals (Ti, Nb, and V) with unsaturated d-orbitals in MXenes. This stabilization facilitates subsequent interlayer bonding via reaction with various metal vapors (Al, Ga, and In) at elevated temperatures, yielding a family of well-defined non-vdW solids with ultrathin layered structures. Moreover, this strategy is readily scalable, enabling the fabrication of a continuous non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film featuring a heterogeneous architecture with a reconstructed MAX-like bonded region and a locally unbonded MXene region. These structural features endow the non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film with exceptional mechanical flexibility, high-temperature oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air, and an electrical conductivity of ∼10 000 S cm–1. Consequently, the film demonstrates an electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness of up to 47.9 dB at a thickness of 5 μm, along with durable infrared stealth performance under prolonged exposure at 500 °C for 48 h.

title:
Tailored ZnO/Cellulose
Separator Reconfigures Solvation
Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
content:
Abstract
Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we first report an inorganic inter-reinforced organic composite separator, fabricated by pairing cellulose with a zinc oxide (ZnO)-enhanced layer and designed to regulate the electrolyte solvation architecture by effectively anchoring solvent molecules. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that the electron-deficient Zn sites on ZnO enhance the solvent-capture ability of the polar hydroxyl groups on cellulose via bidirectional charge transfer. This interaction reconfigures the Mg2+ solvation sheath into a unique single-cluster structure, steering the formation of a dense, ultrathin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that facilitates rapid Mg2+ desolvation while suppressing parasitic side reactions. Consequently, the as-assembled Mg||Mg symmetric cells deliver an exceptional cycling lifespan exceeding 2000 h with minimal overpotential and exhibit robust compatibility across diverse electrolyte systems. This inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy for modulating solvation chemistry offers a generalizable avenue toward long-life and high-safety magnesium metal batteries.

title:
In Situ Ion-Exchange-Mediated
Dynamic Nanointerface
Reconfiguration for Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical–Photothermal
Biosensing
content:
Abstract
Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC–photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay. The Z-scheme heterostructure of a plasmonic Au nanoparticle (NP) layer-supported BiOI/AgI/indium tin oxide glass (BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO) is constructed as the initial photoelectrode. In the sensing process, a CEA recognition event directly reshapes the phase composition of BiOI/AgI, charge-transfer behavior, and photoresponse polarity. The synergistic integration of the BiOI/AgI heterostructure and the close-packed layer of plasmonic Au NPs substantially enhance the light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial charge transfer, making BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO a highly suitable photoelectrode for the PEC mode of the PEC–PT biosensor. This analyte-driven phase evolution reconstructs the semiconductor composition, band alignment, and charge-transfer pathways to switch the photocurrent polarity from cathodic to anodic. In addition, a photothermal imaging mode of the PEC–PT biosensor is triggered by regulating the Bi2S3 formation for intrinsic cross-validation. By integrating an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted analysis, PEC–PT biosensors enable robust multimodal quantification and improved analytical reliability, achieving > 99.8% prediction accuracy in real-sample analysis. This is the first example of integrating a dynamic nanointerface-driven PEC–PT dual-mode biosensor with artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced multimodal analysis for CEA detection and provides a dynamic nanointerface-driven strategy for intelligent multimode biosensing.

title:
Three-Dimensional Covalent
Organic Framework for the
Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
content:
Abstract
We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to < 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

title:
Spin
Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N 2  Reduction on Chiral
Mesostructured Bi 2 WO 6
content:
Abstract
Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: Cost effectiveness of synthetic fuel and CO2 removal for net-zero aviation
content: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.

title: High-frequency inductively heated molten salt bubbling beds for methane pyrolysis
content: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. This study shows that high-frequency magnetic induction directly and volumetrically heats molten salt bubbling beds with stable power delivery, providing a scalable route for methane pyrolysis while managing solid carbon formation. These principles have applicability more broadly to molten salt chemical conversion and thermal energy storage systems.

title:
Calorimetric and Raman Spectroscopic Evaluation of
Mixed Hydrogen–Methane Hydrates: Applicable to Energy Storage
content:
Abstract
Safe and cost-effective storage and delivery of hydrogen (H2) remain critical challenges for the establishment of a hydrogen-based economy. Gas hydrates have emerged as a promising medium for H2 storage; however, their application has been limited by the severe operating conditions required for hydrate formation and stability. In contrast, methane (CH4) hydrates can be stabilized at near-ambient temperatures and moderate pressures. This study investigates mixed H2–CH4 hydrates as a potential way to enable hydrogen storage under significantly milder conditions. Phase equilibrium conditions for mixed hydrates of varying compositions were evaluated using a multicell high-pressure differential scanning calorimeter. Experimental findings were further compared with thermodynamic predictions obtained from Multiflash v6.2 employing the CPA-Infochem equation of state. In addition, the hydrate structures were characterized using an inVia Reflex Raman microscope spectrometer. The combined experimental and modeling results provide new insights into the phase behaviors and structural features of mixed H2–CH4 hydrates, highlighting their potential for practical hydrogen storage applications.

title:
Dynamic Modeling and Pilot-Scale Design of a Chemical
Looping Combustion Reactor Using Red Mud as an Industrial Waste Oxygen
Carrier
content:
Abstract
The use of industrial wastes as oxygen carriers (OCs) in chemical looping combustion (CLC) has gained recent attention as these materials demonstrate the potential to be a cost-effective alternative to synthetic OCs. A key limitation in the development of CLC with industrial waste OCs is the lack of modeling efforts for CLC systems with these materials. This work presents a dynamic multiscale packed-bed reactor CLC model of the oxidation and reduction stages to investigate the performance of red mud, an industrial waste from the alumina refining industry, as an OC. Kinetics describing the oxidation reaction of red mud with oxygen and the reduction reactions of red mud with CH4, CO, and H2 fuels were fitted and assessed using lab-scale experimental data. To further advance CLC with red mud, the packed-bed model is used to design a pilot-scale CLC system, following scaling constraints and design heuristics. The proposed pilot-scale design exhibits moderate utilization of the red mud OC, an average of 89% fuel conversion during the dynamic reduction stage, and is estimated to produce a total thermal energy output of 235.6 kWh. Evaluation of the red mud performance under various reactor conditions at pilot scale provides valuable insights into the potential for this industrial waste to advance CLC toward industrial relevance and adoption.

title:
Phase Equilibria
of CO 2  and CH 4  in Multisalt Brines: Parametrization
and Validation of an Ion-Specific
Electrolyte Cubic-Plus-Association Equation of State
content:
Abstract
We present an ion-specific parameterization of the electrolyte Cubic-Plus-Association (eCPA) equation of state, which we refer to as ms-eCPA, for phase equilibria of CO2 and CH4 in multisalt aqueous brines containing Na+, Cl–, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, and SO42–. The model includes a Soave–Redlich–Kwong physical term with a Huron–Vidal mixing rule, Wertheim 4C association of water with CO2 cross-association, and Debye–Hückel plus Born electrostatic contributions on an ionic basis; the static permittivity is closed self-consistently through the Onsager–Kirkwood relation. The parameterization is hierarchical─each level of added physical description (nonpolar fluids, the associating solvent, ions in the solvent, gases over brine) introduces only parameters fitted to that level’s own data─with the top-level gas–ion interaction energies and ion volume translations calibrated against 1,931 experimental CO2–brine VLE points in five salts (T = 283–473 K, P = 1.3–1200 bar, ms = 0.09–6 mol kg–1), 581 CH4–brine points in six salts (T = 298–598 K, P = 4–1379 bar, ms = 0.25–6 mol kg–1), and 905 high-accuracy brine densities (T = 283–473 K, P = 9–686 bar). A colligative verification of the inherited ion parameters against the Pitzer osmotic-coefficient standard uncovers, and corrects, two defects in the published ion set (the Ca2+ parameters and the Mg2+ polarizability). Across the parametrized range, at salt molalities to 6 mol kg–1, the model predicts CO2 solubility to within 4.3–11.1% AARE per salt and CH4 solubility within 1.6–10.2% AARE per salt, reproduces brine density across the full salinity and temperature range through a temperature-dependent ion-specific Péneloux volume translation with a single ion-additive coefficient set, predicts CO2 solubility in mixed-salt brines with no mixed-brine tuning, and predicts measured calorimetric enthalpies of CO2 dissolution in water and NaCl brines to 0.6 kJ mol–1 with no adjusted parameters. The parameterization provides the thermodynamic basis for subsurface CO2 sequestration and CH4 production in realistic formation brines. In a separate study, the model is paired with robust two- and three-phase stability and flash computations and extended to N2, H2, C2H6, C3H8, and CH4–CO2 gas mixtures.

title:
Bifunctional
Platinum Catalysts on Sulfonated Porous
Aromatic Frameworks for the Hydrodeoxygenation of Furanic and Cyclohexanone-Derived
Precursors to Fuel-Range Hydrocarbons
content:
Abstract
The catalytic hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of biomass-derived oxygenates requires bifunctional catalysts that combine acid and metal sites, yet the reaction networks of polyfunctional substrates remain incompletely understood. In this paper, two bifunctional catalysts based on sulfonated porous aromatic frameworks with different platinum loadings (PAF-30-SO3H–Pt(1) and PAF-30-SO3H–Pt(3)) were prepared and studied in the HDO of two model substrates: 1,1-bis(5-methylfuran-2-yl)cyclohexane (C6-(MF)2) and the condensation products of cyclohexanone. These two substrates represent two classes of biomass-derived SAF precursors─the furanic C6-(MF)2, obtained by alkylation of lignocellulose-derived 2-methylfuran with cyclohexanone, and the self-condensation products of cyclohexanone, a common model compound of lignin bio-oils accessible by partial hydrodeoxygenation of lignin-derived phenolics. Their hydrodeoxygenation yields fuel-range naphthenic hydrocarbons, suitable as SAF components. The catalysts were characterized by CHNS and ICP-AES analysis, FTIR, XPS, N2 adsorption, TEM, and SEM, and the reaction products were identified by GC-MS. The transformations proceeded through the combined action of the acidic SO3H groups and platinum. Additional reaction routes were identified for both substrates, including the formation of methyldecalins and an acid-catalyzed cyclization competing with hydrogenation, which was markedly more favorable for the cyclohexanone trimers, as supported by DFT calculations. Higher temperature, H2 pressure, and platinum loading increased the yield of hydrocarbons, which reached 91% for the cyclohexanone condensation products and 51% for 1,1-bis(5-methylfuran-2-yl)cyclohexane after 4 h of reaction at 250 °C and H2 pressure of 5 MPa. Upon reuse, the catalyst was substantially deactivated, mainly through the accumulation of carbonaceous deposits that blocked the pores, while the framework and sulfonic groups remained intact.

title:
Explainable
Machine Learning Combined with Feature
Selection and Bayesian Optimization for Predicting Rare Earth Elements
and Yttrium in Coal: A Case Study of China’s Five Major Coal-Bearing
Regions
content:
Abstract
Determining the concentrations of rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) in coal is essential for evaluating coal-hosted critical metal resources and understanding their geochemical controls. However, conventional laboratory analyses are costly, time-consuming, and spatially sparse, limiting regional-scale assessment. In this study, we compiled 527 coal samples from 30 coalfields across China’s five major coal-bearing regions and developed an explainable machine learning framework for REY prediction. Unlike previous site-specific models, this framework integrates feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and SHAP interpretation for REY prediction at a broad regional scale. After data preprocessing, multicollinearity diagnosis, and correlation-based feature selection, 16 predictors were retained for model construction. Four ensemble regression models, including Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees (ET), CatBoost (CAT), and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), were optimized using Bayesian hyperparameter search and 5-fold cross-validation. The ET model achieved the best test-set performance among the four ensemble models, with RMSE = 39.962, MAE = 29.669, and R2 = 0.716, although predictions for highly enriched samples remained uncertain because of the long-tailed REY distribution. SHAP analysis identified Ga as the most influential predictor, followed by geological age and P2O5, suggesting that clay-related terrigenous input, stratigraphic context, and minor phosphate-associated phases may jointly influence model-predicted REY enrichment. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can serve as an effective prescreening tool to prioritize coal samples for detailed REY analysis, while independent validation is recommended for high-value target areas.

title:
Selective
SO 2  Absorption in CO 2 -Containing Simulated
Marine Exhaust Gas: Optimization of
Sodium-Based Buffer-Type Mixed Absorbents
content:
Abstract
SO2 removal in marine exhaust gas cleaning systems is evaluated together with the CO2 concentration. Absorbent design must therefore consider selective SO2 removal in the presence of CO2. This study compared the SO2 absorption performance, pH stability, and SO2/CO2 selectivity of NaOH, NaHCO3, and Na2CO3 under SO2-only conditions and in the presence of 8% CO2 using simulated marine exhaust gas. At an equal compound molarity of 0.25 M under SO2-only conditions, Na2CO3 showed the highest conversion retention and pH stability. Its average SO2 conversion was 99.6%, the duration at pH ≥ 7 was 98.6 min, and t90 exceeded 120 min. Na2CO3 also exhibited the highest overall gas-phase mass transfer coefficient, KG, of 8.932 × 10–3 mol·m–2 · s–1 · kPa–1 in wetted-wall column (WWC) tests. In the presence of 8% CO2, all three absorbents maintained approximately 99% SO2 conversion. NaHCO3 showed the highest uptake-based apparent SO2/CO2 selectivity of 0.213. These results guided the design of NaHCO3–Na2CO3–NaOH buffer-type mixed absorbents. The 1%-A and 5%-B formulations were selected from the 1 and 5 wt % groups, respectively, as candidates for subsequent wet scrubber evaluation. Both maintained pH ≥ 7 for 180 min in the bubble reactor. Their apparent CO2 uptakes were 36.6 and 22.9 mmol·L-solution–1, respectively. In the wet scrubber, 1%-A and 5%-B achieved SO2 conversions of 96.5% and 94.6%, respectively, while the outlet CO2 concentration remained close to the inlet level. The study identifies bicarbonate-rich, low-NaOH buffer-type formulations that maintain SO2 removal while showing a small decrease in outlet CO2 concentration.

title:
The Coming
Wave of PV Waste in China: A Systematic
Assessment of Recycling Potentials toward a Circular Economy
content:
Abstract
Solar photovoltaic (PV) is recognized as one of the effective pathways to achieving carbon neutrality, receiving extensive advocacy and the most widespread implementation in China. However, the expansion of the photovoltaic industry has created significant challenges for waste management. Current research on the comprehensive resource potential and sustainable benefits of decommissioned PV systems in China remains insufficient, particularly when climate commitments and PV industry development stages are considered together. Accordingly, this study proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the multidimensional sustainable benefits of decommissioned PV recycling across integrated scenario combinations. The results indicate that (1) by 2050, cumulative decommissioned PV will range from 1164.2 to 1402.7 GW, generating 6.43 × 107–7.86 × 107 MT of resource potential. (2) An estimated 93.83% of the PV waste may consist of PV modules, 6.04% may be inverters, and 0.13% may be cables and brackets. Among these, glass (61%), aluminum (16%), and steel (14%) are projected to constitute the largest proportions. (3) Recycling decommissioned PV could generate cumulative net economic benefits ranging from CNY 903.49 to 1088.60 billion (USD 140.40 to 161.99 billion), save between 2.19 × 108 and 3.81 × 108 GJ of primary energy, reduce carbon emissions by 111.44 to 142.05 million tons of CO2-eq, decrease wastewater generation by 2.52 to 3.43 billion m3, and prevent the accumulation of solid waste by 47.27 to 56.95 billion tons. This study offers valuable insights into photovoltaic waste management and recycling in China, as well as guides other countries facing challenges in the disposal of decommissioned PV systems.

title: Addressing the Zinc Corrosion Conundrum: The Vital Role of Resting-State Kinetics
content:
Abstract
Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have emerged as a highly desirable system for grid storage applications due to low-cost, high-energy density, and safe operating conditions. While AZMB studies often focus on functional mitigation of dendrite formation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), corrosion remains a more ambiguous yet crucial limiting factor in anode performance. Specifically, recent work points to persistent chemical corrosion as a major source of resting capacity loss in AZMBs. In this work, we present a wide-ranging mechanism for galvanic corrosion based on fundamental electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, highlighting the key roles of battery components, electrolyte conditions, and other contributing factors. Importantly, this mechanistic framework also applies when plating and stripping Zn on the anode, offering additional insight into the ever-elusive mechanistic origins of HER during those operating regimes. We then propose several promising avenues of inquiry and methods for further predicting, understanding, and mitigating corrosion in AZMBs.

title: Metal-Dependent Magnetic Exchange Topology as a Fingerprint of N 2  Binding in Isostructural MOF Nodes
content:
Abstract
Triangular metal-oxo nodes are widely employed as catalytic motifs in metal–organic frameworks. Photocatalytic N2 fixation using the all-iron nodes can be switched off by replacing them with all-chromium nodes. However, the two nodes bind N2 in the opposite order to their activity. The present contribution shows that the electronic structure of the metal, which governs the small-molecule binding to the framework, determines the magnetic exchange topology of the [MIII3(μ3-O)] node. Combining broken-symmetry and non-collinear DFT, Hamiltonian-based reconstruction of Mössbauer spectra, and quantitative modeling of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, one finds that FeIII exhibits a genuinely frustrated triangle of comparable antiferromagnetic interactions, whereas CrIII features an asymmetric dimer-plus-monomer governed by unusually strong biquadratic interaction, placing it outside the conventional Heisenberg regime. The distinct electronic structure is reflected in markedly different magnetic topologies and N2 binding strengths, rationalizing the contrasting photocatalytic activities of the two frameworks. These results establish magnetic exchange topology as an experimentally accessible descriptor of chemical function in trinuclear MOF nodes.

title: Structure-Activity Correlation in NiCo 2 X 4  (X = S, Se, and Te) Systems for Electrocatalytic Glycerol Oxidation
content:
Abstract
The overall efficiency of electrocatalytic water splitting is hampered by the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at the anode. This issue can be resolved by replacing the OER with a more thermodynamically favorable glycerol oxidation reaction. Herein, we have synthesized a series of nickel-cobalt-based spinels (NiCo2X4; X = S, Se, and Te) as potent electrocatalysts for the glycerol electrochemical oxidation reaction (GEOR). The trend observed for their catalytic activity toward GEOR is: NiCo2Se4 > NiCo2S4 > NiCo2Te4. A high selectivity of 75.37% and Faradaic efficiency of 83.61% toward formic acid, along with 64.14% conversion of glycerol, is achieved at 1.625 V vs RHE after 24 h using NiCo2Se4. Post-electrocatalysis revealed that NiCo2Se4 acts as a precatalyst and undergoes surface reconstruction into NiCoOOH during glycerol oxidation. Upon integrating the NiCo2Se4 electrocatalyst as both cathode and anode, a two-electrode system for hybrid water splitting (HWS) (HER||GEOR) requires 1.497 V to generate a current density of 10 mA cm–2, which is 470 mV lower than the conventional water splitting (HER||OER). There is a 15.7% reduction in energy consumption in HWS compared to the overall water splitting. Theoretical calculations revealed that the inherent structural asymmetry of NiCo2Se4 is responsible for enhanced activity toward glycerol oxidation, as reflected by a higher interfacial electrostatic potential difference value upon glycerol adsorption than in NiCo2S4 and NiCo2Te4.

title: A Multimodal In‐Situ Liquid Phase TEM and Electrochemical Study on Boric Acid as Electrolyte Additive for Alkaline Zinc‐Air Batteries
content:
This study establishes a multimodal correlative workflow to bridge disparate analytical scales in battery research. By linking dynamic in‐situ liquid‐phase TEM at the nanoscale with microscale morphological analysis and macroscale electrochemistry, a comprehensive mechanistic evaluation of electrolyte additives is achieved. Applied to boric acid, this cross‐scale methodology demonstrates how localized nanoscale phenomena dictate macroscopic device performance.








ABSTRACT
Rechargeable aqueous zinc‐air batteries are critically hindered by dendrite formation, parasitic hydrogen evolution (HER), and corrosion at the zinc anode. Here, we employ a multimodal characterization strategy, bridging nanoscale visualization with macroscale information, to understand the effects of boric acid (BA) as an additive in alkaline media. In‐situ liquid phase TEM (LPTEM) observations demonstrate that BA additive suppresses HER and promotes a uniform, compact plating with highly reversible stripping. This contrasts sharply with the base electrolyte, which shows vigorous bubbling, nonuniform plating, and incomplete stripping. This nanoscale mechanism translates to the macroscale, where BA induces a transformation from dendritic structures to the desirable, compact “boulder‐like” deposit. Macroscale electrochemical analysis quantifies this effect, revealing that 130 mM BA suppresses the corrosion current density by an order of magnitude significantly inhibiting HER. Further investigations combining XRD, ICP‐OES suggest that BA is likely to exist as the tetrahydoxyborate anion, which functions as a non‐consumed, non‐incorporated surface‐active agent. Finally the cycling of ZnO‐PTFE composite anode in BA containing electrolyte over 75 cycles at a current density of 120 mAh/gZn at 30% DOD with 100% columbic efficiency shows the promise of BA as a practical electrolyte additive.

title: Unveiling Hidden Patterns in Electrode‐Electrolyte Interphase Chemistry and Architecture Through Machine Learning‐Assisted Mass Spectrometry Analysis
content:
Electrode‐electrolyte interphases are critical for battery performance, yet their chemical, structural, and thickness heterogeneity are challenging to resolve. Machine learning applied to 3D TOF‐SIMS datasets reveals how individual chemical components shape interphase composition, spatial architecture, and local thickness variations. The approach uncovers patterns hidden in conventional analyses and guides the design of uniform, stable interphases.








ABSTRACT
Electrode‐electrolyte interphases (EEIs) govern battery performance, yet the interplay between their chemical composition and spatial organization remains challenging to resolve. Time‐of‐flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF‐SIMS) provides rich 3D chemical depth profiles of these interfaces, yet conventional analyses simplify the complexity by collapsing the data into 1D depth profiles or 2D maps, obscuring critical spatial features. Here, we apply a machine‐learning‐based approach directly to 3D TOF‐SIMS depth profiles, leveraging their full spatial and chemical richness to investigate the interphase structure and chemistry more comprehensively than conventional analyses. Principal component analysis (PCA) identifies fragments that dominate chemical heterogeneity across the EEI, reveals correlated and anticorrelated spatial distributions, and enables direct comparison of average interphase chemistry and chemical variability. Building on this, t‐distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t‐SNE) and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) resolve stratified structures and fine‐scale spatial interphase variations. Finally, applying PCA to fragment‐specific thickness maps enables comparison of interphase thickness heterogeneity and identifies the chemical species responsible for local thickness variations. Together, the approach creates a generalized framework for extracting chemically and spatially meaningful information from complex TOF‐SIMS datasets, linking interphase chemistry to electrochemical behavior and guiding the design of uniform interphases for advanced battery systems.

title: Mechanistic Insights Into Noble Metal Nanoparticle Antimicrobial Activity through Correlative SEM–SEI‐XPS Analysis
content:
A correlative HR‐SEM/EDX and SEI‐XPS workflow visualizes how silver and platinum nanoparticles interact with bacteria and fungi, revealing species‐dependent structural damage and distinct chemical‐state evolution. Depth‐resolved XPS tracks intracellular nanoparticle transformation, showing AgNPs oxidation and PtNPs stability, providing mechanistic insight for designing durable, ion‐release‐controlled antimicrobial materials.








ABSTRACT
This article presents a correlative analytical strategy for studying nanoparticle–microbe interactions. Understanding the intracellular transformations of metallic nanoparticles (MNPs) provides critical insights into their antimicrobial mechanisms and informs the design of safe, durable antimicrobial materials. Conventional analytical techniques, however, are limited in their ability to simultaneously capture nanoscale morphological changes and the chemical‐state evolution of nanoparticles within microbial cells. To address this, a strategy integrating high‐resolution scanning electron microscopy (HR‐SEM) with sputtering‐enabled intracellular x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (SEI‐XPS) was developed, enabling depth‐resolved, chemically specific analysis of nanoparticle–microbe interactions. Using AgNPs and PtNPs as model systems, their fate was investigated in one bacterium (Arthrobacter sp.) and two phylogenetically distinct fungi (Alternaria obovoidea and Cladosporium sp.). SEM revealed rapid membrane disruption in bacteria and slower, species‐dependent structural impairment in fungi. SEI‐XPS demonstrated biologically induced oxidation of AgNPs, with increasing Ag(I) and higher‐order oxidized species correlating with exposure time and microbial damage, while PtNPs remained predominantly metallic, confirming an ion‐release‐independent antimicrobial mechanism. Depth profiling enabled direct chemical‐state mapping of intracellular nanoparticle residues, revealing persistent metallic cores for both AgNPs and PtNPs. This approach provides mechanistic insight inaccessible through conventional assays and establishes SEI‐XPS as powerful, laboratory‐based method for probing nanoparticle transformations in living microbial systems. The methodology also offers a framework for rational design of next‐generation antimicrobial coatings, including those intended for cultural heritage conservation.

title: Pore‐Stitching Engineering of Biomass‐Derived Hard Carbon for Enhanced Sodium‐Ion Storage
content:
Hydroxyethyl cellulose enables “pore stitching” in demineralized biomass‐derived hard carbon by promoting reconstruction of the etching‐disrupted carbon framework and redistributing accessible pore structures toward micro/ultramicroporous domains. The reconstructed architecture balances impurity removal, structural integrity, and sodium‐storage accessibility, leading to enhanced reversible capacity, improved interfacial kinetics, and stable pouch‐cell performance for practical sodium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Biomass‐derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost‐effective anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non‐metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through‐pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl‐rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen‐containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC‐derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na+ storage domains. Consequently, the optimized HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 375.3 mAh g−1 at 20 mA g−1. A 700 mAh pouch cell pairing this HC with sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7, NFPP) delivers 150 Wh kg−1 based on the combined active‐material mass of both electrodes and retains 97.8% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a viable route for converting impurity‐rich agricultural waste into high‐performance HC anodes for practical sodium‐ion energy storage.

title: Dual Descriptor‐Guided Design of Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes for Stable Zinc Batteries
content:
Guided by hydrogen‐bond saturation and directionality, EOD and MEP are proposed to evaluate polyol HBDs in zinc‐salt‐based eutectic electrolytes. Four C2–C6 polyols are studied, showing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol achieves balanced interfacial adsorption and desolvation kinetics. This work provides polyol HBD design rules for advanced aqueous batteries.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H2O activity and regulate Zn2+ desolvation through hydrogen‐bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn2+ coordination. A series of C2–C6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C4, EOD = 0.022 Å−3, MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery‐enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm−2 with 1 mAh cm−2, and the Zn||I2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.

title: Jahn–Teller Distortion of MnO6 Octahedra Enhances Piezoelectric Polarization and Lattice Oxygen Activation of BaTiO3 for Efficient Piezo‐PEC Water Splitting
content:
A Jahn–Teller effect‐driven strategy was proposed to regulate the local B‐site octahedral structure of BaTiO3 for efficient Piezo‐PEC water splitting. The Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non‐centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn3+ strengthens Ti‐O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water‐splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism toward the lattice oxygen mechanism, thus accelerating reaction kinetics.








ABSTRACT
Piezo‐photoelectrochemical (Piezo‐PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water‐splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn–Teller effect‐driven strategy to regulate the local B‐site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO3 for efficient Piezo‐PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn3+ ions with asymmetric eg orbital occupancy (t2g3eg1), a local MnO6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn–Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non‐centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water‐splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO‐6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 52.3 pm V−1. This work reveals that Jahn–Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo‐polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo‐PEC water‐splitting systems.

title: Nickel‐Free Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Self‐Assembled Monolayers: A Pathway to Efficient and Recyclable Devices
content:
Replacing toxic NiOx with phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole monolayers (Ph‐5PACz) yields inverted perovskite solar cells that are efficient and recyclable. The nickel‐free interface reaches 25.3% efficiency and enables closed‐loop ITO recovery with near‐98% performance retention, while life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses confirm lower energy demand, metal use, and up to 29% reduced environmental impact.








ABSTRACT
High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel‐free hole‐selective interface material based on phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole self‐assembled monolayers (Ph‐nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure‐property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph‐5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried‐interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me‐4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph‐5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel‐free interface enables a closed‐loop recycling route unavailable to nickel‐based devices, with recycled‐ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity‐related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.

title: Self‐Reporting Hierarchical DNA Nanoplatform for Tumor Cell‐Selective Senescence Modulation and Immune Remodeling
content:
A self‐reporting hierarchical DNA nanoplatform integrating a newly engineered senescence‐responsive charge‐reversal lipid carrier with a dual‐input catalytic DNA circuit is reported, enabling multilayered molecular computation and selective senescence reprogramming in pathological tumor cells. The activated circuit simultaneously reports pathological senescence and assembles an NF‐κB decoy to suppress downstream SASP, thereby remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment toward an immune‐active state.








ABSTRACT
Therapy‐induced senescence (TIS) promotes tumor resistance and recurrence through the senescence‐associated secretory phenotype (SASP), but achieving tumor cell‐selective senescence modulation remains a formidable challenge due to limited cellular specificity, insufficient spatiotemporal control, and the complexity of the secretory program. Here, we develop a self‐reporting hierarchical DNA nanoplatform (Gal‐lipo@S‐CHA) that enables selective senescence reprogramming and immune remodeling in TIS tumor cells. In this design, a newly engineered β‐galactosidase‐responsive charge‐reversal lipid carrier establishes the first layer of senescence selectivity by enabling preferential delivery and enhanced endosomal escape of a hierarchically gated catalytic DNA circuit. Subsequent intracellular decoding of GSH and microRNA‐21, two tumor‐associated and senescence‐enriched molecular signatures, provides a second layer of tumor cell selectivity, activating the circuit specifically in pathological senescent tumor cells. The activated circuit simultaneously generates a fluorescence signal for real‐time monitoring and assembles an NF‐κB decoy to block NF‐κB nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing downstream pro‐tumorigenic SASP production at the upstream regulatory source. In vivo studies demonstrate that Gal‐lipo@S‐CHA effectively remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by enhancing natural killer cell infiltration and M1 macrophage polarization. Collectively, this framework establishes a new paradigm for selectively reprogramming pathological senescence, providing a versatile platform to support immunomodulatory cancer therapies.

title: Dense Lithium Deposition on Ultrathin Eutectic Sn–Bi–In Foils by Coupled Diffusion Doping and Dynamic Creep Wrinkling
content:
An ultrathin eutectic Sn–Bi–In alloy foil suppresses Li dendrites via coupled creep wrinkling and diffusion doping, generating a self‑renewing lithiophilic gradient that prevents pulverization and ensures uniform Li deposition.








ABSTRACT
Ultrathin lithiophilic alloy foils (<10 µm) are highly desirable for advancing high‐energy‐density rechargeable lithium metal batteries toward practical applications, particularly in view of the persistent dendrite formation associated with pure Li anodes. Here, an ultrathin eutectic Sn–Bi–In alloy foil is fabricated through a simple melt–cooling–rolling process at 62°C. The foil enables uniform and dense Li deposition with an ultrahigh areal capacity of 200 mAh cm−2 through the synergistic effects of dynamic creep‐induced wrinkling, which guides Li nucleation, and elemental diffusion, primarily of In, which homogenizes the local Li+ flux. The resulting dendrite‐free, columnar Li deposits exhibit excellent plating/stripping reversibility, sustaining stable cycling for 3500 h at 2 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2 with a low overpotential of only ∼13 mV. Full cells paired with LiFePO4 cathodes achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.69% over 600 cycles. These findings establish a scalable electrode design strategy that integrates mechanical adaptability with chemical self‐regulation, offering a promising pathway toward practical high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries.

title: Competitive Coordination to Ether Oxygens Enables High‐Ionic‐Conductivity Solid Polymer Electrolytes at Room Temperature
content:
FeF3 is introduced as Lewis acidic additive that reshapes the Li+ coordination in poly(ethylene oxide)‐based solid polymer electrolyte. Strong Fe3+–O–C interactions weaken Li+–O–C binding and Li–N bonds, promoting salt dissociation and lowering Li+ hopping barriers. The resulting solid electrolyte reaches high ionic conductivity and stable battery cycling under ambient conditions.








ABSTRACT
The practical application of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) electrolytes in solid‐state lithium metal batteries is severely constrained by low ionic conductivity at ambient temperature. To address this intrinsic limitation, we introduce FeF3 as a multifunctional additive into the PEO/poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‑HFP) matrix, yielding the FeF3‑PEOPVLi electrolyte. Fe3+ ions with strong Lewis acidity competitively coordinate with the ether oxygen atoms via Fe3+–O–C interactions, thereby weakening the native Li+–O–C coordination and substantially reducing the energy barrier for Li+ hopping. Concurrently, the strong electron withdrawing nature of Fe3+ promotes lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) dissociation by weakening the Li–N bond, increasing the concentration of free Li+ ions available for ionic transport. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the FeF3‑PEOPVLi electrolyte achieves high ionic conductivity of 0.13 mS cm−1 at 25°C. Solid‐state Li||LiFePO4 batteries deliver discharge capacity of 120.6 mAh g−1 at 0.5 C at 25°C and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work demonstrates that rational modulation of the coordination environment within PEO provides a viable and effective pathway toward high‑performance room‑temperature solid‑state lithium metal batteries.

title: Low‐Frequency Noise and Stability in Electrolyte‐Gated Nanoscale Silicon Field‐Effect Transistor Sensors
content:
Electrolyte‐gated nanoscale silicon field‐effect transistor sensors provide exceptional charge sensitivity and direct electrical readout. However, their sensing accuracy is fundamentally limited by low‐frequency noise and baseline drift. This review examines the origins of noise and drift in these sensors, summarizes the key mitigation strategies, and highlights the importance of coordinated optimization across the transducer, sensing interface, electrolyte/electrode environment, and readout.








ABSTRACT
Electrolyte‐gated nanoscale silicon field‐effect transistors (Si FETs), including silicon nanoribbon FETs (SiNRFETs) and nanowire FETs (SiNWFETs), have emerged as highly promising platforms for chemical and biological sensing. As these sensors move from proof‐of‐concept demonstrations toward quantitative assays, practical performance is increasingly governed not only by nominal sensitivity, but also by their signal‐to‐noise ratio (SNR) and baseline stability. Low‐frequency noise (LFN), typically arising from carrier‐number and mobility fluctuations in the solid‐state device, as well as reversible ion adsorption/desorption processes at the solid–liquid interfaces, is generally characterized by an approximately 1/f‐dependent power spectral density. It limits the minimum resolvable signal and thus determines the limit‐of‐detection (LoD). In parallel, slower nonstationary processes, including ion penetration and reference‐electrode drift, cause baseline instability that complicates quantitative sensing and array calibration. This review discusses LFN and instability in electrolyte‐gated nanoscale Si FET sensors as a coupled device‐interface‐readout problem. Mitigation strategies are also summarized. Representative examples illustrate how dominant noise sources can be identified and suppressed. Finally, we highlight the applications of low‐noise and low‐drift FET sensors. Next‐generation electrolyte‐gated nanoscale Si FET sensors require codesign of the transducer, sensing interface, electrolyte/reference environment, and front‐end electronics to achieve a low LoD and high detection accuracy.

title: Highly Transparent and Fast‐Switching Solid‐State Electrochromic Devices With Nanostructured Solid Polymer Electrolytes
content:
Nanostructured solid polymer electrolytes integrate interconnected ion‐conducting channels with a mechanically robust, transparent matrix. Efficient ion transport through these nanoscale pathways enables electrochromic devices to combine rapid switching, high coloration efficiency, and solid‐state stability, overcoming the conventional trade‐off among liquid, gel, and solid electrolytes for scalable and flexible electrochromic applications.








ABSTRACT
While electrochromic devices employing solid polymer electrolytes offer advantages in safety and mechanical durability compared with conventional devices using liquid electrolytes, their performance is often limited by slow switching speeds and low coloration efficiency mainly due to slow ion transport within the solid medium. To address these challenges, we introduced a nanostructured solid polymer electrolyte (NSPE) featuring high‐density nanoscale ion‐transport channels embedded within a mechanically robust polymer matrix. These nanochannels provide efficient ion‐conduction pathways while minimizing light scattering. Using a complementary WO3/NiO electrochromic configuration, we evaluated the effect of the NSPE architecture on device performance. The resulting device exhibited a high bleached‐state transmittance of 74.5% and a large optical modulation of 63.7% in the visible region. Notably, the device exhibited rapid switching kinetics, with coloration and bleaching times of 11.8 and 2.1 s, respectively, together with a high coloration efficiency of 146.7 cm2 C−1. Furthermore, the electrolyte enabled the successful fabrication of both large‐area (80 mm × 80 mm) and flexible electrochromic devices while retaining electrochromic functionality, highlighting its scalability and mechanical adaptability. These results demonstrate that nanochannel‐engineered solid electrolytes provide an effective strategy for achieving high‐performance, transparent, and mechanically versatile electrochromic devices for next‐generation smart window applications.

title: Asymmetric Interfacial Charge Gradients Enable Dual‐Pathway Proton Transfer for High‐Flux Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
content:
Spatially asymmetric interfacial charge gradients create distinct proton‐transfer domains, enabling surface‐site H* migration at the negatively polarized Ni/Mo2N interface and hydrogen‐bond‐network‐mediated proton hopping at the positively polarized Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interface. This dual‐pathway architecture sustains continuous hydrogen‐intermediate delivery and establishes a resilient interfacial microenvironment for high‐flux alkaline hydrogen evolution.








ABSTRACT
Accelerating water dissociation while maintaining efficient proton transfer remains a substantial challenge in high‐flux alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we introduce an interfacial engineering strategy to develop a high‐flux alkaline HER electrocatalyst with controllable spatially asymmetric interfacial charge gradients, by incorporating size‐tunable Ni nanoparticles at Mo2N/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfacial regions to create a Ni‐nanoparticle‐bridged dual‐interface heterogeneous structure with coordinated proton‐transfer pathways. The resultant electrocatalyst achieves an industrial current density of 1.0 A cm−2 at 1.74 V in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, outperforming commercial Pt/C by 10%, while sustaining 100 h intermittent operation under 10–1000 mA cm−2 current cycling, demonstrating robust operational stability under high‐flux conditions. Such high‐flux HER capability can be attributed to the formation of asymmetric charge gradients along the Ni/Mo2N and Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfaces, which reorient interfacial water molecules into favorable configurations to promote dissociation at apical Ni nanoparticle sites and continuously supply protons. Simultaneously, the generated protons are directed through two coordinated pathways consisting of electrostatically guided surface migration at the negatively polarized Ni/Mo2N interface and hydrogen‐bond‐network‐mediated hopping at the positively polarized Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interface, safeguarding against proton‐transfer bottlenecks and active‐site blockage under high‐flux conditions. This work establishes interfacial charge gradient regulation as a design principle for high‐flux alkaline HER.

title: Antiferrodistortive Matrix Engineering Reprograms Polarization Pathways for Ultrahigh Energy Storage at Moderate Electric Fields
content:
Antiferrodistortive matrix engineering reprograms the polarization evolution pathway in relaxor ferroelectrics by introducing a field‐dependent polarization dormancy–awakening process. The engineered matrix delays premature polarization saturation, extends the nonlinear response window, and enables ultrahigh dielectric energy storage under moderate electric fields, establishing a promising design strategy for designing next‐generation high‐power ceramic capacitors.








ABSTRACT
Relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs) are promising dielectric materials for pulsed multilayer ceramic capacitors because of their rapid polarization response. However, under practical electric fields, polarization rapidly approaches saturation as polar nanoregions exhaust their nonlinear switching capability, fundamentally limiting energy‐storage performance. Here we demonstrate that antiferrodistortive matrix engineering reprograms the polarization evolution pathway through a polarization dormancy–awakening process. Long‐range antiferrodistortive modulation, introduced by the intrinsic lattice instability of CaZrO3 in a (Bi0.5Na0.4K0.1)TiO3 matrix, creates local strain fields that temporarily suppress PNR switching and progressively awaken dormant polarization under moderate electric fields. This substantially extends the nonlinear polarization‐response regime without inducing ferroelectric or antiferroelectric ordering. Atomic‐resolution electron microscopy, electron diffraction, and phase‐field simulations collectively reveal the structural origin of the awakening behavior and its coupling to local polarization dynamics. Consequently, the engineered relaxor ceramic achieves an ultrahigh recoverable energy‐storage density of 12.3 J cm–3 with an energy‐storage efficiency of 87.4% at 520 kV cm–1, representing a benchmark performance for bulk RFE ceramics operating under moderate electric fields. This work establishes antiferrodistortive matrix engineering as a promising design strategy for reprogramming polarization evolution in RFEs toward high‐performance dielectric energy storage.

title: Local Coordination Asymmetry Engineering Activates Oxide Path Mechanism in Dopant‐Free RuO2 for Ultra‐Durable Acidic Water Oxidation
content:
By constructing disorderly connected regular and irregular Ru‐O6 octahedra, we induce local coordination asymmetry that enables oxide path mechanism (OPM) in dopant‐free RuO2. This mechanistic transition breaks the activity‐stability trade‐off of monometallic Ru‐based catalysts, achieving an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV and over 2100 h of operation in a PEM water electrolyzer.








ABSTRACT
Developing ruthenium‐based anode electrocatalysts to replace commercial iridium is crucial for reducing the cost of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis. However, conventional RuO2 suffers from limited long‐term stability and severe overoxidation drawbacks. Herein, we employ dynamic H2 bubble template (DHBT)‐assisted electrodeposition combined with calcination to fabricate disorderly connected regular/irregular Ru‐O6 octahedra. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that this local coordination asymmetry favors an oxide path mechanism (OPM) involving direct O‐O coupling while suppressing *OOH formation and substantial lattice‐oxygen participation. The optimized d‐RuO2‐x catalyst requires an overpotential of only 154 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for over 3200 h at this current density. Crucially, in a PEM water electrolyzer, the catalyst operates robustly for over 2100 h at 200 mA cm−2 under continuous and start‐shutdown conditions. These results demonstrate that local coordination asymmetry engineering can tune OER pathway selection in dopant‐free RuO2‐based catalysts and provide a promising route toward durable acidic OER anodes.
