title:
Redox-Induced Polymeric
Micelle-to-Coacervate Transition
for Enhanced Endosomal Escape, Prolonged Drug Retention, and Improved
Sequential Drug Delivery
content:
Abstract
Polymeric micelles (PMs) and coacervate microdroplets (CMs) are both promising delivery vehicles, yet each suffers from distinct limitations. The delivery efficiency of PMs is often hindered by factors, such as limited endosome escape and uncontrolled drug release. On the other hand, CMs are prone to coalescence and aging, which hamper long-term storage and systemic injection. Here, by employing an intracellular morphological transition strategy, these drawbacks can be efficiently addressed without compromising their inherent advantages. The system exists as nanosized PMs during storage and circulation. Upon internalization by the tumor cells, the highly reductive intracellular environment induces the detachment of the poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) shell and results in in situ formation of CMs. The formed CMs can effectively escape from endosomes by disrupting the endosomal membrane, facilitating the release of drugs into the cytoplasm. Furthermore, the CMs can serve as drug reservoirs, protecting the cargo from burst release and degradation, thus significantly prolonging the retention time and improving systemic delivery efficacy. Notably, the CMs can also sequester free drugs from the surrounding environment, enhancing sequential therapy by increasing the intratumoral accumulation of the temporally staggered agents. Thus, this micelle-to-coacervate transformable platform illuminates new possibilities for both types of drug-delivery systems.

title:
Kinetic Programming
of Heteromolecular Contacts in
Boron- and Nitrogen-Containing π-Systems via External
and Internal Cross-Seeding
content:
Abstract
We establish a kinetic strategy for controlling the supramolecular copolymerization of boron- and nitrogen-containing π-electron systems by exploiting intramolecular hydrogen bonding in cystine-based dimeric diamides. Two dimeric diamides bearing solubilizing alkyl chains, DBB and DNN, were designed and synthesized by functionalization with planarized triarylborane (PTAB) and planarized triarylamine (PTAA) units, respectively. In low-polarity solvents, both molecules form one-dimensional nanostructures upon ultrasonication. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the two diamide units within the cystine framework suppresses spontaneous nucleation and generates metastable monomeric states, thereby providing a kinetic window for seeded supramolecular polymerization. Despite a difference of more than 10 kJ mol–1 between their Gibbs free energy changes for homopolymerization, external cross-seeding with preformed DBB seeds initiates the supramolecular polymerization of metastable DNN monomers. The resulting supramolecular copolymers exhibit long-lived emission arising from spatially confined interactions between the PTAB and PTAA units. The extent of heteromolecular contact formation can be modulated by switching between external and internal cross-seeding protocols. In the internal cross-seeding process, DBB assemblies are generated in situ in the presence of DNN monomers, enabling their incorporation during supramolecular growth and producing coassemblies with an enhanced contribution of heteromolecular excited-state interactions. These results demonstrate that kinetic control over nucleation and elongation enables pathway-dependent regulation of heteromolecular contacts in equimolar binary supramolecular polymers with markedly different homopolymerization propensities.

title:
Giant
Baromagnetic Effect Induced by Spin Engineering
in Mn 3 (Zn 0.25 Sn 0.25 Ga 0.25 Ge 0.25 )C
content:
Abstract
Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. However, the practical implementation of BME is hindered by the small magnetization change and the large driving pressure required in conventional materials. Guided by spin-polarized calculations, this work successfully obtains a giant BME material Mn3(Zn0.25Sn0.25Ga0.25Ge0.25)C, which exhibits a remarkable pressure-induced maximum magnetization change (|ΔMmax|) of 2.63 μB·f.u.–1 and an exceptionally large baromagnetic coefficient (BMC, d) of 15.0 μB·f.u.–1·GPa–1. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. First-principles calculations further clarify that pressure modulates the energy difference (ΔE) between the cAFM and FM configurations via the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, elucidating the microscopic origin of the giant BME. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. It further provides clear guidance for designing materials with superior functional properties.

title: Stepwise Delithiation and Interfacial Electric Field Engineering Enabling Stable Cycling of LiNi<sub>0.8</sub>Co<sub>0.1</sub>Mn<sub>0.1</sub>O<sub>2</sub>/LiFePO<sub>4</sub> Hybrid Cathode Under Harsh Conditions

title:
Wettability Alteration of Coals with Different Coal
Ranks Induced by Fluorocarbon Surfactant FS-61
content:
Abstract
Coal wettability strongly influences coalbed methane (CBM) recovery and water-block damage in coal reservoirs. Wettability reversal from hydrophilic to hydrophobic is therefore an effective approach for improving CBM production. In this study, low-rank long-flame coal, medium-rank coking coal, and high-rank anthracite were selected to investigate the rank-dependent wettability reversal induced by the fluorocarbon surfactant FS-61. Contact angle, surface tension, SEM-EDS, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) were combined with low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and low-temperature nitrogen adsorption to characterize changes in surface wettability, morphology, functional groups, and pore structure. The critical micelle concentration of FS-61 was determined to be 0.3 wt %, and the surfactant markedly reduced the surface tension of the aqueous solution. FS-61 treatment decreased hydrophilic hydroxyl groups and introduced hydrophobic C–F moieties on coal surfaces, resulting in enhanced hydrophobicity. The wettability reversal efficiency decreased with increasing coal rank, with the water contact angle of long-flame coal increasing from 51.70° to above 90%, indicating the strongest modification effect. In contrast, anthracite exhibited a weaker response, which was attributed to its relatively compact pore structure and intrinsically higher hydrophobicity. Nitrogen adsorption showed that FS-61 increased the adsorption capacity of long-flame coal by 248.85% while decreasing that of anthracite by 27.54%, demonstrating a pronounced rank dependence of pore-structure modification. EDS mapping further revealed that fluorine adsorption followed the order of long-flame coal > coking coal > anthracite. FTIR results indicated that FS-61 mainly modified surface functional groups without substantially altering the coal macromolecular framework. Low-field NMR demonstrated enhanced liquid flowback from coal pores after treatment, indicating effective mitigation of water-block damage. These findings reveal the strong dependence of FS-61-induced wettability reversal on coal rank and provide a basis for targeted wettability modification and enhanced CBM recovery.

title:
High-Pressure
Rheology of Waxy Oils: Pressure and
Gas Dissolution Effects
content:
Abstract
Wax precipitation and gelation in high-pressure oil and gas flowlines pose major flow-assurance challenges, but the effects of pressure and gas dissolution on the thermodynamics and rheology of waxy oils remain largely unexplored. In this study, high-pressure calorimetry and rheometry were used to investigate a model waxy oil under two contrasting gas environments: inert helium to isolate the intrinsic effect of pressurization, and oil-soluble methane to capture the combined effects of pressurization and gas dissolution. Under helium pressurization, wax appearance temperature (WAT) and the wax precipitation curve shifted to higher temperatures, indicating enhanced wax crystallization. This, together with pressure-induced liquid-phase compression, increased oil viscosity and gel yield stress. Under methane pressurization, dissolved methane shifted the WAT and wax precipitation curve to lower temperatures, while also weakening liquid-phase intermolecular interactions, thereby reducing oil viscosity and markedly decreasing gel yield stress. Stepwise shear-rate tests revealed time-dependent structural breakdown and pronounced hysteresis under all conditions, with pressure and dissolved methane altering the magnitude of shear stress but not the fundamental breakdown mechanism. Herschel–Bulkley (HB) modeling showed that helium pressurization modestly increased HB-extrapolated dynamic yield stress and consistency index, whereas methane primarily reduced the consistency index with only minor changes in HB-extrapolated dynamic yield stress and shear-thinning behavior. These findings demonstrate that dissolved gas, not merely pressurization, governs live waxy oil rheology and must be explicitly considered in flow assurance design.

title:
N-Doped
Carbon Nanosheet-Confined CoSe 2  Enabling High-Rate and
Durable Sodium Storage
content:
Abstract
Transition-metal selenides (TMSes) show considerable potential as anodes of sodium-ion batteries, benefiting from their diverse redox reactions and large theoretical capacities. Despite these merits, TMSes suffer from drastic volumetric changes and sluggish electron transport, leading to a degraded cycling stability and poor rate performance. Herein, an integrated CoSe2@NC nanoarchitecture was developed through a Co-hexamethylenetetramine precursor-mediated selenization strategy, yielding ultrafine CoSe2 nanoparticles encapsulated within interconnected nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets. The two-dimensional nanosheet morphology maximizes the accessible electrochemical interface and facilitates rapid Na+ migration, while the nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheet serves as a conductive network for efficient electron transport and a structural scaffold that accommodates the volumetric variation. Benefiting from this synergy, CoSe2@NC delivers a considerable reversible capacity, superior rate capability, and robust cycling capability. Quantitative kinetic analyses reveal that the superior performance originates from dominant pseudocapacitive charge storage, lowered interfacial impedance, and accelerated Na+ diffusion. Additionally, CoSe2@NC exhibits a competent performance when assembled into sodium-ion capacitors, further demonstrating its potential for practical sodium-based energy storage.

title: Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Enables Energy-Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide and Carbonate Coproduction from CO-Rich Flue Gas and Air
content:
Abstract
The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. However, COOR has rarely been implemented in practical paired electrolysis systems because of modest device-level performance, reliance on purified CO feedstocks, and operational instability. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Under high-current-density operation, in situ surface analysis revealed that interfacial carbonate accumulation causes anodic passivation and current decay. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.

title: Tautomeric Metal-Polymer Coordination Enables Damage-Free Laminated Carbon Electrodes in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Abstract
Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. However, mechanical stress during lamination and the large work-function mismatch between the CE and the electron transport layer (ETL) can compromise performance. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy utilizing a silver-2-mercaptobenzothiazole (Ag-MBT) metal-polymer buffer layer to enable high-efficiency inverted CE-based PSCs (C-PSCs). XPS reveals Ag-induced changes in the sulfur and nitrogen chemical environments of MBT, consistent with the formation of an Ag-MBT interfacial coordination layer involving Ag–S coordination. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.

title: Unlocking Quantum Confinement in Two-/Three-Dimensional Tin-Based Perovskites for High-Efficiency Photovoltaics
content:
Abstract
Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.

title: Overcoming the Trade-off Between the Activity, Stability, and Cost of OER Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis in a Self-Driving Laboratory
content:
Abstract
Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.

title: Advanced Fuel Cell Catalyst Comprising Hierarchical Three-Dimensional Network Structured Mesoporous Carbon and a Nitrogen-Rich Polymer Shows Remarkable Stabilities against Carbon Corrosion and Pt Sintering
content:
Abstract
Here, a developed hierarchical 3D network structured mesoporous carbon (nwOMC) coated with a nitrogen-rich polymer (poly[2,2′-(2,6-pyridine)-5,5′-bibenzimidazole]; PyPBI) was offered as a catalyst support with high tolerance against carbon corrosion and sintering of metal catalyst. N2 adsorption, XPS analysis, and temperature-programmed desorption measurements showed a dramatic decrease in both the micropore volume and the oxygen-surface functional groups of nwOMC (those are susceptible for electrochemical oxidation) after the PyPBI coating process. The nwOMC tolerance against oxidation increased by 60%. PyPBI played an active role in improving the catalytic activity and durability of the anchored Pt. The Pt mass activity increased by about 67% @ 0.85 V, and the Pt stability against coalescence enhanced by about 2.5. The outcomes of the present study are noteworthy to define a different route toward the development of fuel cell catalysts.

title: Persistent Inter-particle State-of-Charge Heterogeneity in Fast-Charged High-Loading NMC811 Electrodes Revealed by Ex Situ Raman Spectroscopy
content:
Abstract
Designing high-energy lithium-ion battery (LIB) cells based on LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) cathodes that combine high areal capacity, fast-charge capability, and long-term cycling stability remains challenging. Particle de-/lithiation and degradation do not proceed uniformly across composite electrodes or within NMC secondary particles, resulting in inter- and intra-particle state-of-charge (SOC) heterogeneity that can accelerate electrode degradation and limit rate capability. This work introduces an ex situ Raman-based approach to estimate the local SOC in NMC811 particles in ion-milled electrode cross-sections with sub-micron lateral resolution. The method is based on an empirical correlation between SOC and the wavenumber of the minimum/inflection point near 500 cm–1 in the Raman spectra. We investigated high-loading NMC811 electrodes at charge rates from 0.5 to 3C (with 0.1C used for calibration) and after 100 aging cycles at 0.5C. Our key finding is the charge-rate-dependent occurrence of a particle subgroup with Raman-derived SOC values near 0% after open-circuit relaxation. At charge rates ≤1C, the measured particles exhibit a continuous, unimodal SOC distribution across particles, whereas at ≥1.5C, a distinct near-0% SOC particle subgroup is still detectable after >1 h under open-circuit conditions, with Raman signatures consistent with a highly lithiated state. The absence of this near-0% SOC particle subgroup in aged electrodes cycled at 0.5C argues against degradation as the primary origin and indicates that the phenomenon is primarily rate-driven. Overall, this work reveals persistent heterogeneous active-material utilization in high-loading NMC811 electrodes and suggests that fast charging can kinetically isolate a subset of particles or particle regions even after open-circuit relaxation, which may contribute to electrode degradation and capacity fade.

title: From Layered Porous Architectures to Multicomponent Functional Materials: Evolution of Catalytic Design Concepts
content:
Abstract
This Review aims to highlight Avelino Corma’s fundamental contributions to the understanding, rational design, and modification of layered zeolitic materials and to show the evolution of the concepts emerging from this research evolved and inspired the further development of increasingly sophisticated hybrid, multifunctional, and multicomponent porous architectures. The first strategies based on the swelling, pillaring, exfoliation, and delamination of layered zeolites demonstrated that accessibility to active sites could be significantly enhanced while preserving the characteristic high stability and reactivity of pristine zeolites. These advances consolidated key concepts related to accessibility, structural organization, and controlled modification that progressively paved the way to broader design concepts that were subsequently exploited in organic–inorganic hybrid materials and, at a conceptual level, in purely organic porous frameworks, in which active sites, interfaces, and cooperative functions can be intentionally incorporated and spatially organized within rationally designed architectures. The examples recompiled throughout this review illustrate how this conceptual evolution has moved towards multisite catalysis, one-pot multistep reactions and the transition from thermocatalysis towards photocatalytic and energy-related applications. Nevertheless, important challenges remain, on the one hand to the precise control of active-site location and proximity, phase separation, stability with increasing structural complexity and interfacial cooperation; and, on the other hand, the development of advanced synthetic, operando characterization, computational, and data-driven approaches for a deeper understanding and more rational design of functional organic–inorganic hybrid materials. Overall, the evolution discussed here illustrates how concepts emerging from Avelino Corma’s work on zeolite chemistry and heterogeneous catalysis have influenced the development of increasingly integrated and cooperative catalytic materials.

title: Heteroatom-Mediated Functional Carbon Engineering for the Simultaneous Enhancement of Graphitization and Interfacial Stability in LiFePO 4
content:
Abstract
Carbon coatings are indispensable for mitigating the intrinsically poor electronic conductivity of olivine LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes, yet their potential to regulate cathode/electrolyte interfacial chemistry remains comparatively underexplored. Here, we present a multifunctional carbon-engineering strategy in which LiBOB and LiBF4 are incorporated during carbon-layer formation to tailor carbon ordering and surface chemical functionality simultaneously. Raman spectroscopy revealed enhanced graphitic ordering upon addition of the boron-containing precursors, while TOF-SIMS confirmed the preferential incorporation of boron-containing (and, in the case of LiBF4, fluorine-containing) species within the carbon-rich surface region. X-ray diffraction combined with Rietveld refinement further indicated only minor lattice contraction, implying limited incorporation of precursor-derived species into the olivine framework without disruption of the overall crystal structure. The optimized electrodes modified with 0.2 wt % LiBOB and LiBF4 exhibited markedly improved high-rate performance, retaining approximately 66% and 69% of their 0.1 C capacities at 10 C, respectively, compared with ∼53% for pristine LFP. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed substantially lower charge-transfer resistance after prolonged cycling, and XPS and TOF-SIMS analyses demonstrated that the chemically functionalized carbon layers suppress electrolyte decomposition and promote the formation of a more stable cathode/electrolyte interphase. These interfacial benefits translated into significantly improved cycling stability at elevated temperatures and greater resistance to degradation following storage at 80 °C. Of the two strategies, LiBF4-derived B/F functionalization afforded the most pronounced improvement by coupling enhanced carbon ordering with superior interfacial stabilization. Collectively, these results demonstrate that chemical functionalization can transform conventional carbon coatings from passive conductive layers into multifunctional interfacial architectures that concurrently promote electronic transport, regulate electrolyte decomposition, and enhance the thermal durability of LFP cathodes.

title: Synergistic Regulation of Lattice Chemistry and Interfacial Kinetics in High-Entropy O3 Layered Oxides for High-Rate Sodium Storage
content:
Abstract
O3-type layered oxides are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their practical performance is often limited by phase-transition-induced lattice strain and sluggish Na+ transport. Herein, we report a rare-earth-enabled high-entropy O3 layered oxide, NaNi0.3Cu0.1Fe0.2–xMn0.3Ti0.1GdxO2 (x = 0–0.10), prepared by a solid-state route. X-ray diffraction and selected area electron diffraction confirm an as-prepared single-phase O3 framework, with subtle lattice modulation after Gd substitution. The optimized NCFMTG02 delivers reversible capacities of 128.43 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 101.33 mAh g–1 at 5 C and retains 101.3 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles at 1 C, together with an average discharge voltage of 3.210 V, higher than that of the undoped NCFMTG0 electrode. The composition-dependent trend indicates that performance does not increase monotonically with configurational entropy; instead, an appropriate low-level Gd substitution within the high-entropy O3 framework is required to balance lattice-chemistry modulation and reaction kinetics. Galvanostatic intermittent titration technique and scan-rate-dependent cyclic voltammetry indicate faster Na+ transport and lower kinetic overpotential. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows suppressed Jahn–Teller-active Mn3+, increased Mn4+, slightly more oxidized Ni, and an increased high-binding-energy O 1s component associated with changes in the surface/local oxygen environment. These results suggest that minor rare-earth substitution can complement the high-entropy O3 framework by regulating lattice chemistry, enhancing electrochemical robustness, and improving Na-storage kinetics.

title: Interfacial Stability between Li-Metal/Si Composite Anode and Sulfide Solid Electrolytes in Direct Die-Pressed and Isostatically Pressed All-Solid-State Batteries
content:
Abstract
All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) employing Si–Li composite anodes are promising candidates for achieving high energy density and scalable practical applications. Incorporating metallic Li into Si anodes as a compensation source offers a promising approach to compensate for irreversible Li consumption. Nevertheless, the introduced metallic Li must be carefully regulated to provide sufficient Li compensation for the Si anode while preventing excessive reactions with Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (LPSC). Achieving this delicate balance is therefore essential for constructing stable LPSC/Li@Si interfaces. Herein, we systematically investigate the interfacial stability of Li-metal-prelithiated Si anodes in sulfide-based ASSBs under both direct die-pressing and isostatic pressing conditions. Using NCM811|LPSC|Li@Si cells as a model system, we identify the appropriate Li thicknesses for different cell configurations and demonstrate that stable cycling critically depends on directing the redistributed metallic Li into the porous Si electrode rather than into the sulfide solid electrolyte layer. Such interfacial regulation effectively suppresses the continuous decomposition of LPSC and mitigates the growth of interfacial resistance. Benefiting from the optimized prelithiation and pressing protocol, the application of Li-metal-prelithiated Si anodes was successfully extended from direct die-pressed mold-type full cells (mold cells) to isostatically pressed pouch-type full cells, highlighting their potential for practical high-energy ASSBs.

title: Accelerating Interfacial Charge Transfer in CrC/MnCdS Schottky Junction for Photothermal-Enhanced Photocatalytic H 2  Production
content:
Abstract
Construction of Schottky junction with photothermal enhancement offers an effective strategy to mitigate the rapid recombination of charge carriers and enhance interfacial charge transfer efficiency during photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. In this work, a CrC/MnCdS Schottky junction photocatalyst was successfully constructed through the physical incorporation of metal-like CrC nanoparticles and 1D MnCdS nanorods. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the metal-like nature of CrC, enabling the formation of a Schottky junction with MnCdS that generates a strong internal electric field (IEF), which greatly facilitates the spatial separation and migration of photogenerated charge carriers. CrC possesses broad-spectrum light absorption capability and photothermal effect, which enhance the light absorption ability of the composite and increase the local reaction temperature, thereby lowering the hydrogen desorption barrier, and accelerates reaction kinetics. Consequently, the optimized 20%CrC/MnCdS photocatalyst exhibits a superior H2 evolution rate of 2.61 mmol h–1 g–1, which is approximately 2.96 times higher than that of pure MnCdS. The improved photocatalytic activity arises from the synergy between the Schottky junction and the photothermal effect, which markedly improves the charge separation and concurrently accelerates the interfacial reaction kinetics. This work offers a viable approach for constructing high-efficiency photothermally-assisted photocatalytic systems.

title: Multiple-Site Interaction-Driven Coordination Mechanism for Lithium-Ion Battery Cathode Recovery Using Water-Containing Intermediate-Strength Acid-Based Green Solvents
content:
Abstract
Current hydrometallurgical recycling technologies for spent lithium-ion battery (LIB) cathodes predominantly rely on single-site interactions, which suffer from obvious drawbacks including low leaching efficiency, excessive energy consumption, and usage of highly corrosive strong acids (e.g., sulfuric acid and hydrochloric acid). Herein, we propose a multiple-site interaction-driven coordination (MSIC) mechanism for spent LCO cathode recycling from LIBs using water-containing intermediate-strength acid-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The multiple-site interaction arises from the abundant hydroxyl and carbonyl coordination sites in the DESs formed by glycerol and water-containing phosphoric acid. Results show that the proposed MSIC mechanism achieves leaching efficiencies of 94.7% for lithium and 98.1% for cobalt from the LCO cathode under mild intermediate-strength acid conditions. This remarkable performance substantially outperforms conventional single-site interaction-based leaching, which requires harsh strong-acid environments accompanied by severe equipment corrosion and high operational risks.

title: Managing Non-radiative Losses via Energy Alignment and Defect Passivation Using Dual-Functionality Hole-Transporting Materials in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Abstract
Interfaces significantly influence both the power conversion efficiency and long-term stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Small-molecule hole-transporting materials (HTMs) are particularly attractive due to their structural tunability, advantageous electronic properties, and thermal stability, all of which contribute to enhanced device durability. This study reports the rational design of asymmetric small-molecule HTMs featuring donor-acceptor-donor (DKO) and donor-acceptor-acceptor (DKCN) architectures. The study examines defect passivation by central Lewis-base functionalities in HTMs and improved charge extraction in mixed-halide PSCs. Photoluminescence and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy demonstrate that Lewis-base sites coordinate with undercoordinated Pb2+ centers, thereby reducing trap-state density, suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination, and enhancing charge migration. Side-arm engineering is employed to optimize energy-level alignment and hole-transport properties. DKO exhibits superior hole mobility and more favorable interfacial energetics. Consequently, DKO-based PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 22.85%, representing a 7.5% relative improvement over DKCN (21.25%). This enhancement is primarily attributed to a 6.3% increase in short-circuit current density (JSC: 24.47 vs 23.01 mA cm–2). These findings indicate that integrating Lewis-base functionalization with asymmetric molecular design provides a dual-function strategy for defect passivation and interfacial charge regulation, offering a scalable molecular approach for developing high-performance, stable PSCs.

title: Structural Tailoring of Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) Pellets for Enhanced H 2 S Adsorption
content:
Abstract
The elimination of H2S is important for the efficiency of energy production and safety due to its high corrosion and toxicity. While metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising candidates for H2S adsorption, there remains a critical gap between discovery and industrial deployment. This study bridges the scalability gap of MOFs in this field by tailoring the structure of MIL-53(Al) pellets, investigating how pelletization variables dictate structural characteristics and H2S adsorption performance. By elucidating the impact of the pelletization process, this research contributes to the transition of MOF-based technologies from laboratory-scale experimentation to industrial application. We find that pellets comprising 80 wt % MIL-53(Al) and 20 wt % binder, which were subjected to calcination at 400 oC, are beneficial for reversible adsorption of H2S thanks to the maximized surface area and rigid structure. This MOF/binder ratio also enables an uninterrupted extrusion process. Furthermore, exploring various crosslinking agents identifies Fe3+ as a vital additive. This ionic crosslinker not only facilitates the pelletization of MIL-53(Al) but also enhances H2S removal efficiency by inducing partial amorphization and generating additional active sites. Overall, the findings in our work provide guidance for further research on engineering MOFs into macrostructure forms for H2S removal as well as H2S-related applications in practice.

title: 3D‐Nanostructured ITO Enables High‐Loading Prussian Blue Cathodes for Zn‐Based Electrochromic Smart Windows
content:
Transparent nanostructured ITO electrodes prepared by Glancing Angle Deposition enable conformal Prussian Blue electrodeposition, boosting surface capacity and rate capability. Coupled with reversible zinc plating on a zinc frame and ITO counter electrode, the energy‐storage smart window achieves fast optical modulation and improved charge‐storage performance, while an in‐situ rejuvenation mode enhances cyclability.








ABSTRACT
Prussian Blue (PB) is an attractive electrochromic cathode material for aqueous electrochromic energy‐storage smart windows, but its performance remains limited by the low areal capacity of thin‐coatings deposited on planar transparent conductive oxides. Here, we overcome this limitation by combining galvanostatic electrodeposition with 3D‐nanostructured ITO electrodes, enabling conformal growth of PB with high‐loadings, while maintaining mechanical stability and fast electrochemical response. The resulting electrodes sustain charge densities up to 100 mC/cm2 at relatively high rates. When integrated into Zn/PB smart window devices, they enable fast and homogeneous coloration/bleaching with enhanced optical contrast and charge storage capacity, while also exhibiting high cyclability. Device configurations based on reversible Zn electrodeposition onto a transparent ITO counter electrode enable improved control over optical contrast and electric field distribution, while a three‐electrode architecture incorporating a sacrificial Zn anode provides a route toward in situ regeneration of the electrochromic cathode and extended device lifetime.

title: Bionic Structural Design of Multifunctional Flexible Polypyrrole Sensors for Human Health Monitoring
content:
A biomimetic Thalia dealbata‐inspired stable sensor (S@PPy/PDMS) combines pressure and NH3 sensing for multiparametric health monitoring. The microstructured flexible platform captures respiration, pulse, body motion, and low‐concentration exhaled NH3, while enabling machine‐learning gesture recognition. This dual‐functional strategy supports noninvasive respiratory–metabolic assessment, with potential applications in CKD monitoring, smart wearables, and human–machine interfaces.








ABSTRACT
Rehabilitation medicine is an essential component of universal health coverage, while emerging electronic skin offers new opportunities for portable and personalized healthcare. However, flexible pressure sensors still face trade‐offs among sensitivity, detection range, and stability, and gas sensors remain challenged by low‐concentration detection and environmental robustness. Herein, a biomimetic “Thalia dealbata” microstructured hydrophobic polypyrrole/polydimethylsiloxane (S@PPy/PDMS) composite sensor was fabricated through a one‐step template method and controllable in situ polymerization. The biomimetic PDMS microstructure enhances pressure response, while conductive and NH3‐sensitive PPy enables dual‐mode pressure and gas sensing on a single flexible platform. The sensor exhibits a wide pressure range of 0–25 kPa, a high sensitivity of 3.617 kPa−1, and excellent durability over 19 500 compression–release cycles. It also detects NH3 concentrations as low as 1 ppm with stable performance over 60 days. The dual‐functional sensor enables complementary monitoring of mechanical physiological signals, including respiration, pulse, and body motion, together with metabolic information from exhaled NH3. A five‐channel sensor array further decodes numerical gestures with 100% accuracy via machine learning and wireless communication. Integrating respiratory mechanical sensing with exhaled NH3 detection, this platform offers potential for longitudinal, noninvasive multiparametric monitoring, particularly for CKD assessment, human–machine interfaces, smart wearables, assistive technologies, and telemedicine.

title: Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterojunctions Regulation in Ni‐MnO/C Microspheres With Tunable Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
content:
MnO protrusions and Ni particles were confined within a carbon matrix, and their tunable dispersity, size, and content were systematically achieved, enabling precise regulation of dielectric behaviors and electromagnetic wave absorption. Furthermore, by integrating the composite into metamaterial designs and thermally conductive flexible films, an effective absorption bandwidth of 12.28 GHz and heat transfer application were realized.








ABSTRACT
Heterojunctions engineering is crucial for optimizing dielectric polarization and electromagnetic (EM) wave absorption, yet precise spatial control over semiconductor components in magnetic‐dielectric microspheres remains challenging. Herein, super‐dispersed MnO protrusions and Ni particles were confined within a carbon matrix, constructing unique Ni‐MnO/C microspheres via a pyrolysis‐controlled strategy. Leveraging differences in oxygen affinity, MnO protrusions and Ni particles with tunable dispersity, size, and content were systematically achieved, enabling precise regulation of dielectric behaviors and EM wave absorption. The optimized Ni‐MnO/C composite achieved an outstanding minimum reflection loss of ‐51.49 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.20 GHz. Significantly, by further integrating the composite into metamaterial designs and heat‐transfer flexible films, the EAB was dramatically broadened to 12.28 GHz, and thermal insulation was realized. This work introduces a morphological‐engineering strategy that not only overcomes the dispersion‐control bottleneck in heterojunctions design but also bridges the gap between microstructural tailoring and practical device applications, offering a new idea for high‐performance EM wave absorption materials.

title: Non‐Perturbative Bacterial Identification Directly From Solid Agar Plates Using Raman Micro‐Spectroscopy and Machine Learning
content:
This work demonstrates a simple, rapid bacterial identification directly from unopened solid agar culture that neither perturbs culture conditions nor requires extrinsic labels, promising seamless integration of Raman spectroscopy into clinical and microbiology laboratory workflows. The proposed direct Raman measurement combined with machine learning enables characterization of Escherichia coli (E. coli) colonies with minor genetic modification across different agar and petri dish materials.








ABSTRACT
Raman spectroscopy is a promising tool for microbial identification, yet its implementation in microbiology and clinical workflow is still restricted due to the accompanying additional preparation required to focus on microbial signals. Here, we demonstrate Raman‐based bacterial identification directly from unopened, inverted agar plates, the same conditions used during incubation. Our approach enabled sensitive identification using two Escherichia coli variants, differing only in green fluorescent protein (GFP) expression, across diverse media and substrate material conditions, despite the interrogation path traversing 3–4 mm thick background material. We integrated traditional density functional theory (DFT)‐based material computation with machine learning analysis, achieving over 97.7% classification accuracy, surpassing the performance of standard measurements from opened plates by 10.8% higher mean accuracy and 0.76% less variance. We further demonstrated Raman mapping‐based colony identification via Raman peaks characteristic to GFPmut3 chromophore structure generated by DFT. Our approach is robust to changes in algorithms or substrate materials and promises real‐time, non‐perturbative monitoring of bacterial growth, biofilm formation, and antimicrobial resistance development.

title: A π‐Conjugated Polymer Anode With Railway‐Like NH4+ Pathways for High‐Rate Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
content:
Engineering efficient NH4+ transport pathways within electrodes remains a key challenge to achieving high‐performance energy storage in aqueous ammonium‐ion batteries (AAIBs). In this work, railway‐like NH4+ transport pathways are constructed by uniformly aligned carbonyl groups within linear slits between rigid polymer backbones. The resulting AAIB exhibits excellent rate capability, delivering high energy density even at ultrahigh power densities.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous ammonium‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are promising energy storage systems, while the relatively large size and tetrahedral geometry of NH4+ present challenges for its transport within electrodes. Herein, poly(5,8‐diaza‐1,4‐naphthoquinone) (PANQ) has been synthesized to facilitate NH4+ transport in AAIBs. The π‐conjugated PANQ possesses a rigid, linear molecular structure. The straight intermolecular slits with uniformly distributed carbonyl sites form railway‐like NH4+ pathways, enabling rapid ion transport through the dynamic formation and disruption of hydrogen bonds. The PANQ electrode delivers a high capacity of 286.8 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 in a 2 mol L−1 ammonium acetate electrolyte. Thanks to the rapid NH4+ transport pathways, the electrode displays an excellent rate capability, retaining 161.7 mAh g−1 at 80 A g−1. Moreover, it displays exceptional cycling stability over 10 000 cycles at 20 A g−1. The PANQ electrode was employed as the anode in a PANQ//NiCo‐LDH AAIB (NiCo‐LDH represents the Ni‐Co layered double hydroxide cathode), retaining an energy density of 25.2 Wh kg−1 even at an ultrahigh power density of 23 320.2 W kg−1. This study provides a high‐performance electrode candidate for AAIBs and a strategy for constructing rapid ion‐transport pathways to enable efficient NH4+ storage and superior electrochemical kinetics.

title: Label‐Free YaxAB Nanopore Fingerprinting of Cancer‐Associated Single‐Residue Bcl‐xL Variants
content:
A YaxAB nanopore workflow enables label‐free single‐molecule fingerprinting of Bcl‐xL variants. Combined normalized current blockade and noise features generated reproducible current fingerprints for wild‐type Bcl‐xL and the cancer‐associated N136K and R165W variants across independent pores, with WT and N136K remaining distinct despite a mass difference of only 14 Da. Analyte‐specific capture rates provide a concentration‐dependent readout that supports low‐concentration detection.








ABSTRACT
Resolving cancer‐associated protein variants remains difficult when variants share similar molecular masses and folded structures. Conventional assays often require labels or provide ensemble‐averaged readouts, limiting their ability to resolve subtle variant differences. Here, a YaxAB nanopore workflow is presented for label‐free single‐molecule current fingerprinting of wild‐type Bcl‐xL and the cancer‐associated single‐residue variants N136K and R165W. Individual Bcl‐xL proteins were electro‐osmotically trapped within the funnel‐shaped YaxAB lumen, where they generated characteristic ionic‐current events. These events formed reproducible, analyte‐specific event populations in normalized current blockade and current noise space, resolving wild‐type Bcl‐xL, N136K, and R165W as distinct single‐molecule current fingerprints. Wild‐type Bcl‐xL and N136K remained distinct despite a mass difference of only 14 Da, and the fingerprint separation was consistent with combined differences in excluded volume, net charge, and dipole moment. Concentration‐dependent capture‐rate analysis further supported sub‐nanomolar to low‐nanomolar detection corresponding to protein amounts in the sub‐picomole to low‐picomole range, while capture‐rate normalization brought the estimated concentrations closer to the nominal concentrations. These results present YaxAB nanopore sensing as a label‐free single‐molecule workflow for the current fingerprinting of cancer‐associated single‐residue Bcl‐xL variants, with low‐concentration detection as a supporting analytical capability.
